pairs: Qui tetigerit picem inquinabitur ab ea:
Whoever touches pitch will be contaminated by it.
et qui communicaverit superbo induet superbiam.
And whoever associates with the arrogant will be clothed by arrogance.
Pondus super se tollat qui honestiori se communicat,
Whoever associates with those more honorable than himself sets a burden on himself. And so,
et ditiori te ne socius fueris.
you should have no fellowship with someone who is wealthier than you.
What will the cooking pot have in common with the earthen vessel?
And when they collide with one another,
The rich man has suffered no injustice,
But the poor man, though he has been wounded, will remain silent.
et ipse non dolebit super te.
and he will not grieve over you.
If he has need of you, he will deceive you;
et subridens spem dabit, narrans tibi bona,
he will give you hope. He will converse with you pleasantly,
Et confundet te in cibis suis,
And he will impress you with his foods,
donec te exinaniat bis et ter:
until he has drained you two or three times,
and in the very end, he will ridicule you.
And afterward, when he sees you, he will abandon you,
et caput suum movebit ad te.
and he will shake his head at you.
Attende ne seductus in stultitiam humilieris.
Be careful. Otherwise, having been seduced into foolishness, you will be humiliated.
Noli esse humilis in sapientia tua,
Do not choose to be low in your wisdom, otherwise,
having been brought low, you will be seduced into foolishness.
If you are invited by someone who is more powerful than you,
ex hoc enim magis te advocabit.
you should decline. Otherwise, he will invite you all the more.
You cannot be rude to him,
et ne longe sis ab eo,
And you cannot stray far from him,
Ne retineas ex æquo loqui cum illo,
You cannot hold a discussion with him as with an equal.
You should not trust his many words.
ex multa enim loquela tentabit te,
For by much talking, he will probe you,
et subridens interrogabit te de absconditis tuis.
and while smiling, he will question you about your secrets.
Immitis animus illius conservabit verba tua:
His cruel mind will store up your words;
and he will not spare you from affliction,
and attend diligently to what you are hearing.
For you are walking toward your own destruction.
Yet truly, while listening to these things,
consider it as if it were a dream,
Love God for your entire life,
et invoca illum in salute tua.
and call upon him for your salvation.
Every animal loves its own kind;
sic et omnis homo proximum sibi.
so also every man loves those closest to himself.
Omnis caro ad similem sibi conjungetur,
All flesh will join with whatever is similar to itself,
et omnis homo simili sui sociabitur.
and every man will associate with whomever is similar to himself.
If a wolf would at any time have fellowship with a lamb,
so also would a sinner have fellowship with the just.
Quæ communicatio sancto homini ad canem?
What fellowship does a holy man have with a dog?
aut quæ pars diviti ad pauperem?
Or what portion do the wealthy have with the poor?
the wild donkey is the prey of the lion.
So also are the poor the pasture of the rich.
Et sicut abominatio est superbo humilitas,
And just as humility is an abomination to the arrogant,
so also does the rich man abhor the poor man.
Dives commotus confirmatur ab amicis suis:
When a wealthy man has been shaken,
he is strengthened by his friends.
But when a lowly man has fallen,
he is expelled even by those who know him well.
When a rich man has been deceived, many will help him recover;
When a poor man has been deceived,
et non est datus ei locus.
and no place is given to him.
et verbum illius usque ad nubes perducent.
and they repeat his words, even to the clouds.
Bona est substantia cui non est peccatum in conscientia:
Substance is good for him who has no sin on his conscience.
et nequissima paupertas in ore impii.
And poverty is called very wicked by the mouth of the impious.
The heart of a man changes his face,
the sign of a good heart and a good face.
